title: Tumor dissociation of highly viable cell suspensions for single-cell omic analyses in mouse models of breast cancer
protocol: Avoid areas containing necrosis and lymph nodes during tumor harvesting.
Harvest tumors in a clean area using sterilized scissors and forceps, wiping surfaces and instruments with a 70% ethanol solution.
Euthanize mice with CO2, followed by cervical dislocation.
Harvest tissue from epithelial mammary carcinomas, collecting only regions with high content of viable tumor cells.
Exclude necrotic areas and lymph nodes during tissue collection.
Perform a quality control (QC) step to select the highest quality samples.
Avoid bias due to necrosis or lymphocyte contamination in sample selection.
Manually dissect the tumor tissue into 3–5 mm pieces using a surgical scalpel blade.
Chop the dissection into 100 μm pieces with maximum blade force on a McIlwain Tissue chopper for 2–3 passes.
Place the chopped tissue in a 15 mL-Falcon tube containing 4.5 ml of 5% FBS/DMEM High glucose.
Incubate the tissue for enzymatic digestion for 1 hour per sample or 1.5 hours for eight samples at once.
Add 500 μL of collagenase-hyaluronidase (10×) to the sample in a 15 mL-Falcon tube with 4.5 mL of 5% FBS/DMEM High glucose.
Incubate at 37°C shaking at 200 rpm for 30 min in the Incu-Shaker™ 10 L Shaking Incubator.
Disrupt tissue by pipetting up and down with a p1000 set at 1 mL, at least 10 times after 15 min of incubation.
Wash the sample by adding 10 mL of cold DPBS to neutralize the digestion.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 100 μL of DNase solution.
Add 750 μL of TEG, pipette up and down for 1 min at 37°C in the water bath.
Fill up to 15 mL with 2% FBS/DPBS.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Add 1.25 mL of Dispase solution to each pellet and incubate for 5 min in 37°C in the water bath.
Resuspend the pellet in 50 μL of DNase solution and 450 μL of 2% FBS/DPBS.
Add 2 mL of RBC lysis buffer, resuspend, and incubate at 37°C in the water bath for 2 min.
Fill up to 15 mL with 2% FBS/DPBS to neutralize.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 5–10 mL of cold 2% FBS/DPBS.
Filter into 50 mL-Falcon tubes using a 40 μm cell sterile strainer.
Count cells as explained in the cell count and viability step.
Prepare a single-cell suspension of 1 × 106–1 × 107 cells/mL.
Take between 50–150 K cells for QC by flow cytometry.
Fill up to 300 μL with 2% FBS/DPBS.
Optional: Add 3 μL of 50 μg/mL DAPI before running the sample in the flow cytometer to verify viability after checking FSC and SSC.
Set a flow cytometer instrument.
Place the sample in the flow cytometer.
Acquire and/or record ∼100,000 events.
Categorize the cell preparation based on FSC and SSC profile.
Transfer highly viable tumor samples from step 22 into a 5 mL-FACS tube.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of Dead Cell Removal microbeads.
Incubate for 15 min at 20°C–22°C in the dark.
Prepare fresh 1× Annexin V Binding buffer by diluting 100 mL of 10× Annexin V Binding Buffer with 900 mL of RO Water.
Label two extra 5 mL-FACS tubes as negative and positive fraction.
Switch on and set up the autoMACS® Pro separator according to the manual instructions.
Equilibrate the column on the autoMACS Pro Separator with 1× Annexin V Binding buffer.
After 15 min of incubation, dilute the sample to 800 μL by adding 700 μL of 1× Annexin V Binding buffer.
Place the diluted sample and collection tubes in the 5 mL-rack from autoMACS® as explained in the manual.
Separate the live population (negative fraction) from dead cells using the DepleteS program on the autoMACS® Pro separator.
Clean up and shut down the autoMACS® Pro separator following manufacturer’s instructions.
Optional: Check the live fraction separated by autoMACS under flow cytometry using DAPI at a final concentration of 0.5 μg/mL to corroborate high viability of the cell suspension.
Transfer 2.5–5 × 10^6 cells from highly viable tumor samples into a 5 mL-FACS tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in a final volume of 500 μL of a solution containing 2% FBS/DPBS and anti-mouse CD45 antibody at the recommended dilution.
Incubate on ice for 30 min.
Prepare the collection tube by adding 100 μL of FBS to one 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
After the 30-min incubation, wash the sample by adding 1 mL of 2% FBS/DPBS.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant the contents of the tube to discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 2% FBS/DPBS.
Keep the sample on ice and in the dark until FACS sorting.
Set up the nozzle size at 100 μm on the BD FACSAria™ III sorter.
Select the cellular compartment in the FSC-A and SSC-A dot plot for gating strategy.
Exclude doublets using FSC-A and FSC-H.
Select the negative fraction for DAPI.
Gate the positive cells for CD45 and mCherry.
Add 10 μL of 50 μg/mL DAPI to the sample.
Incubate the sample with DAPI for 3–5 min.
Insert the DAPI-stained sample in the sample injection chamber of the BD FACSAria™ III sorter.
Adjust voltage for FSC, SSC and the lasers for the fluorophores used.
Insert the collection tube on the sort collection chamber.
Set up the desired number of events to collect, considering a 50% loss as the “worst-case scenario.”
Recommend setting up the desired number of events to 200 K when aiming for 100 K cells.
Sort CD45+ DAPI- cells (live immune cells).
Sort mCherry+ DAPI- cells (live cancer cells).
Sort CD45-, mCherry-, and DAPI- cells (live stromal cells).
Count the total number of sorted cells.
Prepare the recommended cell concentration for single-cell applications using a 0.4% Trypan blue solution.
Place a glass cover on the central area of a hemocytometer.
Adjust the cell concentration of your sample to be within the range of 2.5 × 10^6–2 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Dilute the sample with 2% FBS in PBS Buffer if it is too concentrated.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C and resuspend in less volume of the used buffer if it is too diluted.
Resuspend the sample by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Take 5 μL with a p20 pipette and mix with 5 μL of Trypan blue in a new tube.
Place the 10 μL mixture in a hemocytometer by positioning the loaded p20 pipette on the glass of the hemocytometer, close to the glass cover edge and releasing the sample carefully.
Count the cells right after adding the trypan blue.
